name: tabular_nested_cv
title: Nested cross-validation, HalvingRandomSearchCV, permutation_importance, learning_curve and sklearn's own cross-fitted TargetEncoder - six correct idioms that all look like leaks
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-tabular: the model-selection false-positive trap

forbidden.why: the only fit call in this file is search.fit at line 98, on train_x, and `search` is a HalvingRandomSearchCV whose estimator is a Pipeline - the search refits every step inside every fold. Nothing is fitted outside a Pipeline or a search object
test_x reaches predict_proba at line 119 and nothing else; permutation_importance at line 103 is given train_x, not the holdout

the estimator handed to cross_val_score at line 88 is a GridSearchCV over a Pipeline, and the estimator handed to learning_curve at line 110 is that Pipeline - in both cases every fold refits the imputer, the scaler and the target encoder. This is nested CV, the shape MLV103's fix prescribes
the policy table has no timestamp: vehicle_age and driver_age are durations, and nothing parses a date, converts one or sorts by one
the only metrics are roc_auc_score and average_precision_score, both in the score-metric carve-out, and both are fed a predict_proba column
roc_auc_score at line 121 is fed model.predict_proba(test_x)[:, 1] from line 119, a score column rather than a hard label

seed_everything() seeds random and numpy at lines 55-56, the split and all three StratifiedKFold objects carry random_state=SEED, and the classifier, the target encoder, the halving search and permutation_importance each carry random_state=SEED
train_test_split at line 79 and every StratifiedKFold (lines 84, 85, 94, 109) pass random_state=SEED
there is no torch in this project and no hand-written gradient step
model.eval() is a torch idiom with no sklearn equivalent
torch.no_grad() has no meaning in a scikit-learn program
no device is ever named in this project
nothing is pickled or loaded here

notes: sklearn.preprocessing.TargetEncoder (line 67) is the sharpest trap in the file: it reads y during fit, which is the surface MLV101's TARGET de-rate exists for, and it is nevertheless correct here because it cross-fits internally (cv=5) and because it is a ColumnTransformer step inside the Pipeline the search refits per fold. A hand-rolled target encoder in the same position with no cross-fit would be a real defect, and no rule distinguishes them.
